problems.description: 36 naming violations across every core source file (index.ts, build.ts, cli.ts): snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants. Being baked into the greenfield foundation, they will compound across the 5-story sessions. Mechanical score 0.55 confirms.
SonarQube cognitive complexity +25 over only +4 functions in a scaffold commit — core logic starts life over-complex, well above typical greenfield levels.
SonarQube reports +2 bugs and +2 smells in the initial scaffold, leaving latent defects to carry into later sessions.

Discrepancy: AST diff reports +0 classes yet convention violations flag class/interface naming in 3 files — the naming linter and AST counter disagree on what constitutes a class; worth reconciling in the measurement stack.

strengths: Idiomatic jest.config.js with ts-jest preset, node test environment, and scoped tests root
Commits package-lock.json, ensuring reproducible dependency resolution across sessions
Well-matched toolchain for a static site generator (commander + gray-matter + marked) — architecturally sound choice
Small, focused diff outside the generated lockfile (~645 lines of real code over 4 functions)
commit_reviews.summary: A decent greenfield SSG scaffold (good toolchain, proper lockfile) whose 36 foundational naming violations — a snake_case/PascalCase breakdown in every core file — sink the convention score to 0.55 and seed debt that the remaining story sessions will inherit.

problems.description: No test files changed; the new TemplateEngine, custom template/layout loading, and the new --templates CLI path are exercised without automated coverage.

Default page/index/layout sources are now embedded as raw Handlebars strings in TypeScript, duplicating markup previously written as template literals and making the defaults harder to diff against the on-disk templates they emulate.

Adding handlebars@4.7.9 pulls a new runtime dependency (plus minimist/neo-async/source-map/uglify-js transitive) for a rendering feature that was previously dependency-free; promotes uglify-js and wordwrap from dev to prod edges in the lockfile.

strengths: Extends the existing build pipeline cleanly by threading an engine through renderPage/renderIndex rather than rewriting the render path
Per-page frontmatter template/layout selection is consistent with the existing gray-matter parsing pattern for title/date/tags
The --templates CLI option mirrors the established --content/--output option style with sensible defaults
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped feature addition that cleanly layers Handlebars templating onto the existing builder, though it ships with no tests for the new rendering surface.

compounding_issues: Session 4's refactor left a vestigial `DevServerPlugin` (empty class) — the dev server remains a standalone `startDevServer()` calling `buildSite` directly, so it was never actually wired into the plugin pipeline it was supposedly refactored into

The session-2 hand-rolled regex-based Handlebars/EJS engines persist through all 5 sessions; the EJS path uses `Function('context', 'with(context){...}')` (eval-style execution), a latent code-injection risk that was never replaced with real libraries

Orphaned dead code accumulates: the original auth-API seed `index.ts` (with a contradictory 'NestJS-like Auth API' doc comment) remains at repo root and is never deleted, alongside compat shims (`src/server.ts`, root `plugins/*.ts`) that split the final tree between root-level and src-level files

Session 5's render-cache skip in `TemplatePlugin` keys on a global `context.stats.pagesSkipped > 0` condition and relies on the subtle invariant that only skipped pages carry `renderedHtml` — functional but fragile; a changed page whose hash differs can still reuse stale cached HTML if the guard is tripped by another page
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the unrelated auth-API seed and scaffolded a fresh `src/` project with CLI entrypoint, tsconfig/jest config, and a first test — establishing a clean base

Session 2 built a dependency-free regex-based Handlebars/EJS template engine with partials and layouts instead of pulling in real template libraries, trading two dependencies for a permanent custom maintenance surface
Session 3 integrated a dev server as a standalone module (chokidar watch + debounced rebuilds + WebSocket live-reload + path-traversal guard) rather than folding serving into the build core

Session 4 re-expressed the whole system as a plugin pipeline (`onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd` hooks with a shared `BuildContext`), shrinking the core `src/index.ts` from ~300 to ~80 lines and shipping the parser/templater as first-class plugins

Session 5 added incremental builds via sha256 content-hashing + template-hash fingerprinting persisted to `.ssg-cache.json`, threading cache/stats through `BuildContext` and adding `--incremental`/`--clean` CLI flags
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the five sessions. Session 1 established disciplined scaffolding and the first test; Session 2 added a substantial, well-tested templating feature (growing tests to cover Handlebars, EJS, partials, and layouts); Session 3's dev server is competent production code with debounced rebuilds, live-reload, and path-traversal protection; Session 4 was a strong architectural refactor that cut the core module by ~75% and introduced a clean plugin abstraction; Session 5 capped the arc with hash-based incremental caching backed by thorough invalidation tests (test suite grew from 1 to 6 cases spanning parse, build, both template engines, and cache invalidation). The only stumbles are cosmetic-to-moderate: the plugin refactor left a vestigial DevServerPlugin and stray compat shims, the custom eval-based template engine carried a latent security risk to the end, and the cache-skip logic leans on a fragile global guard — none of which blocked the progression.
story_review.summary: A coherent greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc that steadily improved architecture and test coverage, marred only by leftover dead code and a partially-applied plugin refactor.
